title: Night words everywhere
hookLine: Compline for Christians, the bedtime Shema for Jews, Kirtan Sohila for Sikhs: many traditions close the day with words

cards: Think of a child being tucked in. There's almost always a little ritual: a story, a song, the same few words every night. Grown-ups tend to drop that.
But across the world, whole traditions never did. They close the day with words, in the very last minute before sleep.

teach.b: Start in a monastery. For centuries, Christian monks and nuns have ended the day with a short service called Compline, from a Latin word for completion. After it, many keep a great silence until morning.
Psalm four is sung at Compline in many places, and it holds a line that fits the hour: "I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep." Now a Jewish home.
The Torah says to speak its words "when thou liest down, and when thou risest up."

So at bedtime, many Jews say the Shema, Hear, O Israel, with other prayers that ask for a peaceful night. It's called the bedtime Shema, and children often learn it first. Now a gurdwara, or a Sikh family at night.
They recite Kirtan Sohila, five short hymns from the Guru Granth Sahib, by Guru Nanak, Guru Ram Das and Guru Arjan.

teach.h: THE DAY IS CLOSED, NOT DROPPED.
teach.b: It's read at night, when the scripture itself is put to rest for the night, and at funerals: the day closing and the life closing held in the same words.
And many Muslims, following the practice of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, recite the last short chapters of the Qur'an before sleep.
Each tradition has its own reasons, its own words, its own faith behind them, and each deserves to be understood on its own terms.
But notice the shared shape. The day doesn't just stop. It's closed, like a door, with a few words said the same way every night.

how: Many Christians pray Compline or night prayers, many Jews say the bedtime Shema, many Sikhs recite Kirtan Sohila, and many Muslims recite the last chapters of the Qur'an before sleep, each in their own words.

practice: Choose one line to close tonight with: if you pray, a line from your own tradition's night prayers; if not, a plain one works, the day is done.
Say it inside slowly, as if the lights were already off, and let the week gather behind it: the walk, the scan, the shoulders down, the bedtime, the dim lamp. Then rest in the quiet after the words.

wordCard.voice: Compline, the Christian service from a Latin word for completion, that closes the day with song and prayer. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew, shema: hear. the first word of the Shema, said at bedtime in many Jewish homes.

carryVoice: Your line: the day is done. Next, the path turns toward other people. Sleep well.
